sources.note: No Waerana-specific stress statement. Waerana data (from the Verheijen & Dadu 1994 KITLV typescript) appears only in comparative wordlists (pp.~115-125, 163). The only stress remark is areal, p.115 sec. 3.2.1.2: 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables.'

sources.note: The only grammar sketch of the language (Glottolog's sole descriptive reference; Asplund 2020: 9 calls it the one existing description of Kolor). Pusat Bahasa sketches of this series usually contain a short phonology chapter with a 'tekanan' (stress) paragraph, so this is where a first-hand statement most likely exists. Not digitised anywhere reachable: Google Books VqG1tAEACAAJ no preview; Badan Bahasa repository (repositori.kemdikbud.go.id) unresolvable by automated download -- worth retrying from another network, and requesting via ILL (Cornell/ANU/KITLV hold Pusat Bahasa series).

sources.note: The only substantial lexical documentation of Waerana (source of all Waerana forms in Grimes & Edwards 2026); Verheijen's dictionaries of Manggarai and Rembong carry orthographic/pronunciation notes, and this typescript may include a note on accent. Unpublished; Leiden University Libraries special collections.
